Go - vist - make a donation !!
title: Remarkable work is done here

body: If you want to pay to see a man beating underweight baby elephants with a stick whilst trying to drink the so little amount of milk given to them then go ahead. The babies were trying to go get more milk but they couldn't due to been hit each time they tried. A sign says 'cash! Donation for powdered milk would be appreciated' (what about the 500rp entrance fee Al 40 of us paid!)and every evening people visit! We had to walk away! Whilst trying to get a refund, the men at the reception claim they need beating because they are wild animals! They say they don't get released until they are 4-5 years old!This is not normal! You could see a local man stood behind nodding his head and agreeing with everything we said.
title: Revolting!!!!!!!!!

body: I was so saddened when we visited the Elephant Transit Home a few weeks ago. The elephant keeper, obviously inexperienced and with no empathy what so ever used a white stick to beat the baby elephants to get them to move way from the feeding bottles which contain human formula and not animal formula. MOst of the baby elephants are visibly too thin, many have diarrhoea and are apparently very week. this is an inhumane facility and should not be supported unless strict changes are implemented by the people in charge at the facility, the vet in charge there and the the Department of Wildlife welfare. These elephants are not properly cared for either nutritionally or emotionally. they obviously have o idea what they are doing!
title: lack of animal welfare and visible animal abuse

body: The baby elephant orphanage/transit point is about a ½ hour drive from the Grand Udawalawe Safari resort . This is a must see attraction where baby elephants come for their daily drink of milk every 3 hours. What a great service where these majestic creatures are rehabilitated and reintegrated to the wild.
title: Phen baby elephnts rehabilitation and intgration to the wild

body: Visited the ETH instead of others because of the fact that here, they work to not only save and look after the so many orphaned babies and youngsters but also to ensure (as stress-free as possible (due to very limited human contact) their rehabilitation into the wild when they are ready for it. This, we were told, can take an average of 7 months. It’s very sad to see the sheer number of orphaned elephants - and the reasons for this - which you can appreciate when driving through the island when we’ve seen several wild elephants walking along the road, at the edge of forests and in fields near villages - but very uplifting to see them being fed and enjoying life, playing and learning to be themselves. When we were there, the tourists were pretty well behaved and quiet , which was great. Only saw the staff using a stick once or twice on that visit, which seemed to be to guide them away from the feeding station. Have heard awful things re the treatment of the elephants in the Pinewalla supposed ‘sanctuary’ as well as others!Also went to see lots of elephants roaming freely, on a 3 hr safari at Mineriya National Park which we enjoyed so much - amazing, so intelligent and such caring creatures! Wonderful sight to see them going into and playing in the watercourse. Definitely recommend this visit too.
title: So many elephants

body: We were so torn weather to go or not as treatment of elephants is super important to us and know some places are super iffy. This is one of them. If you want to go watch some underweight, baby elephants being hit with a stick whilst being allowed 20 seconds of milk (before being hit with a stick to leave), this is the place for you. What was more worrisome is that people may say that a poke with a stick may not harm the elephants but many of the elephants shied away from the guy with a stick (tall, slim with glasses) and ran away on seeing him. So either more goes on from what we see, or it does hurt them. Save your money, go to a safari instead and look at elephants in their natural habitat.
title: Not sure why this has so many good reviews

body: Such a wonderful sight to see apart from the worker with the stick, but I guess they are wild animals.... I really hope it's not just a tourist attraction to make money I do know people that have opted not to visit here because of that....We watched the 6pm feed that had more locals not a coach in sight.
title: Hopefully a genuine place not just a tourist attraction

body: This is really a viewing platform where you watch the elephants run in for their feed, drink their milk and play about in the mud and water. And the elephants keep coming! So many of them, about 40 or 50 baby elephants although some of them are older. One has a prosthetic (wooden) leg and it is quite amazing to see him and how he manages. The transit home does marvellous work looking after these unwanted elephants and it seems churlish to criticise at all. We were lucky that our tour guide for our Jules Verne tour holiday was with us and able to explain all that was going on. It would have been nice if we could have met the staff and heard individual tales of each elephant. However, we were fairly close to the elephants and got some amazing pictures in the half hour or so we were there. Definitely worth a visit.
title: Lots of baby elephants!

body: We visited The Transit Home and were very impressed with their work. We saw feeding time for the young elephants which was very comical. We also met an elephant with prosthetic leg. He was absolutely amazing and managed very well with his prosthetic limb. It was quite miraculous to see.Without this place many young elephants may not survive in the wild but thanks to this programme they can be looked after until they are fit and ready to be set free into the National Park.Amazing work guys keep up the good work.
title: Exploring Sri Lanka

body: Good work is being done here and you ticket price goes to buying expensive elephant milk formula, of which the guzzle litres of the stuff daily. They had 45 youngsters being acclimatised for reintroduction into the wild. Feeding time is a joy and enjoyed by both children and adults alike. The Information hall is large and a little space but there are nuggets of information to be gleaned. Well worth the visit.
title: Good

body: The elephants are undeniably cute and it’s heart wrenching to see so many of them orphaned. It’s a worthy cause but the staff can’t seem to care less. It would be great to have the staff tell you about their conservation efforts and I’m sure this would translate to more donations. There’s also not a lot of point to have a sign requesting silence when it’s not enforced and it’s disappointing to see so many disrespectful visitors. That said I would recommend a visit and it’s quite unforgettable watching a baby elephant come running in to be fed and their disgruntled cries when the milk runs out. Their joy in wallowing in the water after feeding is undeniable.Really depressing to see on the drive in along the lakeside to the ETH locals selling food to feed to the elephants (under the signs that ask you not to!). Surely the local police or staff from the ETH could monitor people selling food and people feeding elephants as it all seems a bit of a vicious circle other wise.
title: Mixed thoughts

body: What a lovely experience to sit and watch the gorgeous baby elephants line up to get their milk and grass fed to them. (Some of the babies didn't have a clue how to eat the grasses and kept missing their mouths!)Wasn't there for long but it was very cute.We went after our safari to the 6pm feeding and there wasn't many people there.
title: So many babies

body: Saw the babies having their milk, also some eating leaves & having a wash in the lake. They are so cute, such a shame their has to places like this to take care of orphaned baby elephants, keep up the great work
title: Baby elephant feeding time

body: Visited at feeding time after a safari. Great viewing platform which unsurprisingly gets pretty crowded. So entertaining to watch the babies come in to be fed, splash around on the water and general socialise with their older counterparts. Loved it!
The elephants looked to be so happy and really well cared for. Excellent facilities. Good area to learn as well. We did the morning viewing - plenty of shaded area to avoid the sunshine.
title: Lovely way to spend a morning!

body: You’re only there for about half an hour, it’s cheap and it’s really worth doing if you’re in the area. It’s so cute seeing all the elephants running in for their feed and then playing afterwards. We really enjoyed it.
title: Loved it!

body: Always a bit dubious about these sort of places but I can honestly say the elephants seemed happy.We only saw one juvenile elephant being hit with a stick and that was because he had had his milk and would not move away from the feeding station and was being a bully to some smaller elephants.None of the handlers were trying to manipulate the elephants so the tourists could get better photos, in fact they looked like they weren't bothered if we were there or not.A bonus was some baby owls nesting in a tree as you approach the viewing area.
title: Elephants seemed happy

body: One of very interesting visit in Srilanka. A very well maintained transit home for baby elephant whom mother either died or lost the baby in jungle.Visiting hours are during feeding time when they got feed milk. It's a beautiful event watching 30 baby elephant carrying and cranking like childrens.Must visit to support this unique cause if you are nature and wildlife lover.
title: A must visit home of more 30 baby Elephant

body: Called in here to see the abandoned baby elephants. Very interesting to see how they are managed. The keepers make a good show at feeding time giving the babies milk from a pipe and funnel. Good work being done here to reintroduce them back into the wild.
title: Tour.

body: This was the perfect way to spend the morning!! It was only 500 rupees and we were there for about half an hour. Amazing opportunity to see the elephants being fed!! The transit home is attached to the national park so the elephants can come if they choose. Seemed really ethical and it was great to see all the baby elephants!! I would highly recommend!
title: Worthwhile!

body: They charge just 500 rupees per person worth visiting you can see many baby elephants drinking milk and romaine around
title: Worth visiting

body: Our children aged 7,9,11 absolutely loved visiting the Elephant Transit Home. Get there early to get a good seat on the right hand side out of the direct sun. You can watch them setting up and all the little babies eagerly awaiting their bottles of milk. The information centre was closed when we were there due to Sri Lankan New Year, but if it's open you can make donations. A lovely morning.
title: Very interesting for the kids to see

body: A very short visit and information centre closed. Nice to see so many locals enjoying their day out!
title: Shorter than we expected. Information closed

body: We came here briefly one evening to watch the milk feeding of the orphaned baby elephants. The cost was 500rupees each for us to go in. The feeding lasted in total about 15minutes but it was so cute to watch them get fed and then run over to eat some leaves before heading back. Some elephants were a bit cheeky too which was funny to watch. Also outside the park there are a few nice shops and stalls selling souvenirs of elephant type things. Would definitely recommend.
title: Evening feeding tome

body: Visited before going to udawalawe. I never go to anywhere with captive animals but I was assured they all get returned to the wild. In two minds I went in. The elephants wher all age's some really young. It was nice seeing them feed. The people watching do not get involved in the feeding and you are unable to touch them. I think a good thing. I'd recommend a visit
title: Released

body: It was great experience to watch the little jumbos having their milk meals & enjoying around. but observation pavilion was fully crowded & too hot as it was sheltered with aluminium sheets. Felt elephants were bit too far & babies didnt get attracted much. But overall a good experience.
title: Good Place, poorly managed

body: Seeing all these wild animals getting nurtured at ETH was very special. We got to know that this is one of the most successful transit homes in the whole world. Of course we'd never forget the tiny little baby elephants who came running for milk. Such a special place.
title: Some baby elephants are as cute as ever

body: This is a really worthwhile project that nurtures elephants until they reach an age that will allow them to survive in the wild, at which time they are released.The transit home is not setup for the amusement of tourist so don't expect to get involved with the feeding process or be up close and personal with the elephants.Ignore any review that mentions mistreatment at this place, the reviewers obviously don't understand what is required to manage these amazing creatures.We were fortunate enough to see an elephant in the National Park the next day that was raised in the transit home. Keep an eye out, they have a leather necklace.
title: Great Project

body: While the park does a good Job with orphaned Elephants, you get to see them been feed but its a bit far away , also they are scared of the handler with his stick so guessing they have been trained in some sort of way as to what the stick is , all in all was a good experience - is worth going for a look , should be someone telling you a bit about what is going on would make it more enjoyable
title: They do a good Job

body: This is a fantastic Conservation project. We saw the baby elephants being fed at breakfast time which was just incredible. What an absolute privilege to see these amazing creatures being so well cared for. Too many places are still taking advantage of these magnificent creatures so it was very heartening to see them in this situation.
title: Fabulous

body: It was a delightful experience to see these beautiful creatures being fed and we saw no evidence of any cruelty as mentioned in some reports. Expect to sit or stand in a stepped observation area and to be charmed!
title: Delightful

body: Arrived early to get a good seat (not in the sun facing the feeding area) The baby elephants are very cute with some really little ones who had to feed from a bottle rather than the usual hose and funnel.Didn't last long but its well worth a visit there must be over 30 small elephants all wandering around after being led in in smaller groups. They all feed then eat leaves opposite the seating area before being led out in single file not quite trunk to tail but pretty close to it.If you like baby elephants (and who doesn't?) then you just have to visit this place they are absolutely adorable!
title: Lots of Adorable Baby Elephants what's not to like?

body: Visited sri Lanka two weeks ago and were taken to to the see the elephants ,was not dissapointd we were up very close ,what a wonderful sight to see ,would highly reccomend a visit if you love the elephants
title: Safari visit

body: A good place for orphaned elephants. The ETH takes care of the elephants before being set into the wild. The entrance fee is 500LKR, and it is stated (the ETH is controlled by the Sri Lankan Ministry of Wildlife) that all the money goes back to elephants. As the quote is not very high, additional donations is always highly appreciated. Those animals (few months old elephant babies, elephants with prosthetic legs) really need people's care and help. They also work with a foster parent’s plan, so it is also possible to pass money to raise one of the orphan elephants.This is the only orphanage endorsed by Born Free where elephants are treated with respect, love, and concern.To ensure the successful integration of the wild elephants the public may not touch, bottle feed, get close to or pose for pictures with baby elephants. Nevertheless, the milk feeding is a joy to watch and pictures may be taken from the observation platform.
title: watch the elephant being fed and enjoy them acting in a natural environment.

body: I thought that, in contrast to other places I have been to, the elephants were not made into performing animals. The young elephants, which live wild in the Park, are fed several times a day with milk containing necessary supplements. The crowd can watch from basic seating, not too close to the elephants. Lovely to see these elephants being cared for. It doesn't take a long time to visit and as far as I could see there was no benefit in getting up early, we had a good view at the lunch time feed.
title: Great Place - caring

body: Ignore the one bad review here if someone who doesn’t understand what they have to do to ensure all the elephants get their fair share of milk. I amAn animal and wildlife lover and there is NOTHING cruel going on at this place at all!Basically - all the keepers do with their sticks is TAP the larger “teenage” elephants in order to get them to move out of the way once they have finished their milk and not hog their space. Most of the time they don’t even need to tap them, they just talk to them and usher them away with a gesture. Some of these elephants are tiny - maybe only a couple of months old. Although they are in the same group as the others they are too small and easy for the larger ones to push aside - so they are fed differently and individually. I think this is a fantastic place who are trying to do the right thing. Let’s face it 500 rupees is the cost of a beer. Without that money those orphan elephants would be left to fend for themselves and probably die. I will visit every time I come to Sri Lanka.
title: Fantastic place - their know how to look after ALL the elephants

body: We went to one of the 3 feedings you can watch daily. I cannot recommend going here as we saw - being a bit early - how even the smallest baby elephants were repeatedly hit with sticks on their legs, head and body in order to keep them from rushing in to get fed. They were clearly underfed so must have been hungry. There were at least 200 people there, paying 500 LKR pp, three times daily. That is more than enough to take good care of them. I can’t see how these social and intelligent elephants, that we’re clearly afraid of the keepers, are socialized in a healthy way like this and can be released into nature like this. Very upsetting. Please don’t visit!
title: Very upsetting, advise not to go!

body: Our first experience of Elephants in Sri Lanka. A transit home for orphan elephants. A shaded area for you to watch as the baby and young elephants wait patiently for their turn to get their milk. Lovely to watch them interact with each other and their careers. Once they had drunk their milk they wondered nearer to us to eat leaves great place to get photographs.

body: Have heard a lot of complaints about this place,I could see nothing wrong in what they were doing.As they let the young elephants through for milk it was a joy,ears flapping and trumpeting their way to the milk station. There is a large sign that says "it's quiet in the rainforests so please stay quiet"words to that effect,and I could not believe that visitors could not shut up for the short while it took to feed the elephants,so disrespectful.

body: Daily feeding of orphan elephants. Wonderful seeing humanitarians caring for these babies. Hilarious watching the different personalities of the elephants and how quickly they adapt to the process.Worth a visit before going on safari
title: Lots of baby elephants. So cute.

body: we stopped here on the way to uda walawe national park. the feeding is twice a day and your close enough to see and hear them very well
title: Great if you want to see young orphaned elephants

body: take time to support their important work helping baby elephants including watching feeding time........

Saying that its still great to see milking time and would highly recommend going to see this spectacle as times it was very funny with the Elephants trying to bet back for more milk and the others 'shouting'at the gates to be let in!!These Elephants are returned to the wild into the Udawalawe Safari Park once they are old enough.A great experince.

It was lovely to watch the little ones line up and come up one by one to be fed their first dose of milk followed by some branches to complete their breakfast. There was even one adult elephant who had sadly lost one of its legs and was fitted with an artificial one to help him get back to normal. A great centre that is helping to preserve the local elephants and care for the orphan babies before releasing back into the wild or one of many national parks on the island

body: I loved seeing all the young elephants at feeding time. It was fun to see all their personalities. Thanks
